authoredSolutions.1: Each of the four columns carries a quarter of the load. \[F = \frac{Mg}{4} = \frac{50 \times 10^{3} \times 9.8}{4} = 1.225 \times 10^{5}\text{ N}\] The load-bearing cross-section is an annulus of outer radius \(1.00\text{ m}\) and inner radius \(0.50\text{ m}\): \[A = \pi\left( R^{2} - r^{2} \right) = \pi\left( 1.00^{2} - 0.50^{2} \right) = 0.75\pi = 2.356\text{ m}^{2}\] \[\text{strain} = \frac{\text{stress}}{Y} = \frac{F}{AY} = \frac{1.225 \times 10^{5}}{2.356 \times 2.0 \times 10^{11}} = 2.60 \times 10^{- 7}\]
authoredSolutions.2: For an equilateral triangle of side \(a\), the perpendicular distance from the centroid to each side is \[r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{3}} = \frac{0.09}{2\sqrt{3}} = 0.02598\text{ m}\] Each side is a finite straight conductor subtending \(60^{\circ}\) on either side of the foot of the perpendicular, so it contributes \[B_{1} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{4\pi r}\left( \sin 60^{\circ} + \sin 60^{\circ} \right) = \frac{10^{- 7} \times 1.5}{0.02598} \times \sqrt{3} = 1.0 \times 10^{- 5}\text{ T}\] All three sides give fields in the same sense, so \[B = 3B_{1} = 3 \times 10^{- 5}\text{ T}\] With the current flowing clockwise, the right-hand rule puts the field into the plane of the triangle.
authoredSolutions.3: Each sphere contributes its own moment of inertia about its centre plus a parallel-axis term. With \(m = 1.5\text{ kg}\), \(r = 0.5\text{ m}\) and each centre a distance \(d = 2.5\text{ m}\) from the axis, \[I = 2\left( \frac{2}{5}mr^{2} + md^{2} \right) = 2\left( \frac{2}{5} \times 1.5 \times 0.25 + 1.5 \times 6.25 \right)\] \[I = 2\left( 0.15 + 9.375 \right) = 19.05\text{ kg m}^{2}\]
